Who sends the Durham property tax bill

One county department handles the whole city. Durham County Tax Administration lists property, assesses it and collects the money, while the City of Durham only decides its own rate. You can visit in person at 201 East Main Street, 3rd Floor, Administration Building II, Durham, NC 27701, any weekday from 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM, or call 919-560-0300.

The county splits the office into six areas: License and Fees, Payment and Collections, Personal Property, Real Property, Tax Help and Tax Relief. Mailed payments go to Durham County Tax Collector, PO Box 3397, Durham, NC 27702-3397. Never mail cash. When a parcel goes to foreclosure, the plaintiffs are the City and County of Durham together, so a bill from either side ends up in the same collection process.

Durham tax rates

For fiscal year 2026-27 the city rate is $0.4371 and the county rate is $0.5792, a combined $1.0163 per $100 of assessed value. Rates reset each year when the budgets wrap up in mid to late June, and the new figures start July 1.

City and county rates by fiscal year
Fiscal yearCity rateCounty rateCombined rate
2024-2025$0.5962$0.7987$1.3949
2025-2026$0.4371$0.5542$0.9913

The county reappraised real property effective January 1, 2025, which is why the rates fell between the first and second rows. A parcel inside the City of Durham Business Improvement District pays a combined $1.0863 for 2026-27. A solid waste fee of $185.00 applies for the 2026-27 year, and Morrisville, Cary, Raleigh and Chapel Hill each have their own separate lines.

Due dates and penalties

Bills carry a September 1 due date, but you have until January 5 before interest starts. From January 6, interest runs 2% for the first month and three quarters of one percent for each month after that, as set by G.S. 105-360.

  • A January 5 that falls on a weekend moves the cutoff to the next business day.
  • Monthly payment plans cover real property only and must be set up before the bill goes delinquent.
  • Escrow accounts usually send their payment in late November.
  • Cards add a processing fee, while online electronic checks cost nothing.
  • A returned check costs $25, and from then on the office wants cash or certified funds only.
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to appeal your Durham assessment

Appeals go to the county Board of Equalization and Review. Call Tax Administration for the current filing cutoff, since it changes with each reappraisal cycle and each year's calendar. The county prefers the online appeal on its Tax Help page, which lets you message staff and track your case. A paper form is the fallback.

Durham appraised all real estate as of January 1, 2025. Staff will talk about the appraised value and nothing else, so size of the increase, affordability and service levels are off the table. Outside a reappraisal year, a parcel's value changes only for things like rezoning or new or altered buildings. If you lose before the county board, you have 30 days from the mailing of the decision to notify the state Property Tax Commission, under G.S. 105-290.

Homestead and relief programs

The county describes three homestead programs, plus help through the Department of Social Services for low income owners. Applications are due June 1. Call 919-560-0300 with questions.

  • An elderly or disabled exclusion, with a one time application and a $38,800 income cap.
  • A circuit breaker deferment that holds tax to a percentage of income and needs a fresh application every year.
  • A disabled veteran exclusion of up to $45,000 of appraised value.

Deferred circuit breaker tax is repaid when the owner dies, sells or moves, and the most recent three years come due. If you are selling with a deferment, ask the assessor for the balance early.

What happens when Durham property tax goes unpaid?

Taxes you do not pay on real property turn into a lien on the house. After notices and a pre-foreclosure letter, the county can hand the file to a private attorney and foreclose under G.S. 105-374. The owner of record on the delinquency date, January 6, appears in a required newspaper notice, and a payment plan does not prevent that.

  • Bank attachment: your bank holds the account for ten days, or until the tax office says the debt is paid.
  • Wage garnishment: the employer withholds 10% of gross pay each pay period, as the statute provides.
  • State refund setoff: the state takes the refund and tacks on a $5.00 fee plus a $15.00 administrative fee.
  • Sheriff levy: the sheriff can seize and sell personal property, and a towed vehicle adds a $75.00 towing fee.

Once a file is assigned to an attorney, the tax office stops taking direct payments. The payoff must cover taxes, interest, fees and costs, and it is paid through the attorney. Sales happen once a month, on the second Tuesday at 12:00pm, inside the Durham County Judicial Building lobby at 510 Dillard Street. The winning bidder puts down 10%, then a 10 day upset bid window opens. Until the court confirms the sale, the owner can still redeem. Durham County sells no tax liens, because the legislature ended that practice in 1983.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling a Durham home with taxes owed

The January 1 owner gets the bill for that whole year. If a bill reaches you after the sale, you are told to hand it to the buyer, so agree on the split before closing instead of trusting the mail. Your closing attorney can divide the year between you and the buyer.

  1. Request a written balance from the tax collector first, then choose your closing date.
  2. If the parcel has already gone to a foreclosure attorney, get the payoff quote from that attorney. Only the attorney can give it, so plan the closing date around that quote.
  3. If you have deferred circuit breaker tax, ask the assessor for the amount that comes due on transfer.
  4. Have the closing attorney pay any balance from your proceeds at the table.

A cash buyer can often close fast enough that a payoff quote stays valid, and a cash sale skips the lender appraisal and underwriting steps. The tax lien still has to be cleared first either way.

Durham housing snapshot

The city counts 305,561 residents as of July 2025, a 7.6% gain over 2020. About 52.3% of homes are owner occupied, with a median value of $392,800. Middle household income is $81,619, and gross rent in the middle is $1,508. Those home values are the base the tax rates above apply to.

Frequently asked questions

What is the deadline to pay Durham property tax without interest?

Pay by January 5. Interest starts January 6, even though the bill itself is dated for September 1. Registered vehicles follow a separate schedule.

Who sets the Durham property tax rate?

Both. Council fixes the city portion in its June budget, and the county commissioners fix theirs. You see one combined bill, with new rates starting July 1.

Can I get a payment plan for my Durham property tax?

Yes, for real property only, and you must sign up before delinquency. Before January 5 you may also pay in installments with no agreement at all.

If I sold my Durham house in March, who owes that year's bill?

You do, on paper, because the owner of record on January 1 is billed. The county suggests forwarding it to the buyer, so work out who pays what at closing.

How do I stop a Durham tax foreclosure?

Ask the assigned attorney for a redemption figure and pay it in full before the court confirms the sale. A federal bankruptcy filing can also pause the process.

Who values and bills property tax in Charlotte?

Mecklenburg County's Office of Tax Administration values every parcel in Charlotte and collects the county's tax, and the City of Charlotte's own property tax rides on the same bill. A total bill includes a municipal tax from Charlotte or one of the six county towns, plus county and municipal solid waste fees where they apply. Payments go to the City-County Tax Collector.

The office values parcels, collects property tax and business gross receipts tax, and runs relief programs. Appeals, relief applications and the revaluation all go through the county. City Council's part is the city rate, which it sets in its yearly budget.

You can pay by a toll-free card line at 1-800-994-1026 that answers day and night, by mailed check to a Charlotte post office box, by bank eCheck, or at the counter during weekday office hours. A payment with no 24-digit bill number in the account box is rejected and returned. Cards carry a vendor fee of $3.95 on Visa or Mastercard debit and 2.35 percent (minimum $1.95) on other cards, while eChecks carry none. Payments started from your bank may take as long as four business days to post.

Rates and key dates

The Mecklenburg County rate is 49.27 cents on each $100 of value for FY2027, unchanged from FY2026. The city rate comes on top of it for property inside Charlotte, and the figure for a given year appears on your bill and in the city budget.

Charlotte and Mecklenburg County property tax figures
Charge or dateDetail
County rate, FY2026 and FY202749.27 cents per $100
Last general revaluation2023
Next revaluation2027, then every four years
Informal review after a revaluation noticeAsk within 30 days of the date printed on the notice
Tax due dateSeptember 1, interest-free through January 5

The city's FY2027 budget proposal included a 1.89 cent increase dedicated to public safety, so check your bill for the final city rate.

How to contest a Charlotte tax value

Your Formal Appeal Form goes to the county Office of Tax Administration, and the board of equalization and review hears the case. In a normal year the deadline is the board's adjournment date each spring. The only exception is for owners who receive a notice of value change, who may file by the later of adjournment or the last date to appeal on the notice.

  • File by email to the county's appeals address, by mail to Mecklenburg County BER Real Property Appeals, P.O. Box 31127, Charlotte, NC 28231, or in person at 3205 Freedom Dr, Suite 3500, Charlotte, NC 28208.
  • Back-up documents must arrive with the form or within 45 days of filing it. Anyone other than you or an attorney who speaks for you needs a signed power of attorney.
  • Expect the hearing notice roughly a month before your slot, and send any request to reschedule in writing within ten days of that notice.
  • The board's ruling comes by mail within a month of the hearing. Anyone who still disagrees can go to the Property Tax Commission in Raleigh, within 30 days.

The burden sits with the owner, who must show the tax value substantially exceeds market value. No revaluation-year appeal can be filed before notices of value go out, and the county expects the notices and refreshed online records in early 2027.

Between revaluations, the county keeps the prior value unless a ground in G.S. 105-287(a) applies. Those grounds are clerical or arithmetic mistakes, a misapplied schedule of values, physical changes to the land or buildings, and a change in legal use.

Homeowner relief programs

Mecklenburg County runs the state homestead programs from its tax relief page, and its FY2027 budget carries $3.5 million for the county's HOMES program for qualifying homeowners. A Charlotte owner applies to the county for all of them.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the taxable amount drops by $25,000 or half the appraised value, whichever is more. Owners must be 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled, with income inside the cap, which is $38,800 for 2026.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: takes $45,000 off the appraised value. The application is Form NCDVA-9, and age and income do not matter.
  • Circuit breaker: the portion of the bill above 4 or 5 percent of income is deferred, with the percentage set by where income falls between the cap and $58,200. The deferred amount is a lien and, on a transfer, comes due together with the prior three years.

Income is defined broadly and counts every source except family gifts and inheritances. The county takes Form AV-9 applications until June 1 ahead of the tax year.

Taxes at closing

Closing clears any balance from your proceeds, since the debt stays with the parcel. The lien arises January 1. A house sold in March therefore already owes that year's tax, though September 1 is months away. Treat that year's amount as a payoff line.

Interest starts after January 5: 2 percent for what is left of January, and three-fourths of a percent for each later month. Long nonpayment lets the county file a court action modeled on mortgage foreclosure, with an auction sale. An owner can redeem ahead of confirmation by paying everything owed. The tax office site also hosts a Delinquent Taxpayer Lists page.

For the deed, the seller (transferor) pays the state excise tax to the Mecklenburg County register of deeds ahead of recording. Your closing attorney can confirm the stamps and filing charges that will show on the settlement statement.

To prepare, ask the Office of Tax Administration for the balance on your 24-digit bill, and check whether a circuit breaker deferral or other relief is on the parcel, since a deferral adds prior years to the payoff. Pass both numbers to the closing attorney before signing a contract. With a cash buyer there is no lender payoff, and the tax just comes out of proceeds at the table.

Charlotte housing at a glance

Charlotte's July 1, 2025 estimate is 964,784 residents, a 10.3 percent gain on 2020. Owners occupy 51.0 percent of homes, which leaves renters with almost half. A typical owned home was valued at $385,700 for 2020-2024.

The 2027 values will draw on four years of sales since 2023. If you list in early 2027, keep an eye out for the notice mailing. The new assessment shapes later tax bills, and a buyer may ask about it.

Frequently asked questions

What is the property tax rate in Charlotte?

The county levy is 49.27 cents on each $100 of value, unchanged for FY2027. Charlotte adds its own city rate for property inside the city, set by City Council each year. Your bill shows both, along with any solid waste fee.

When is the next Charlotte revaluation?

The next one lands in 2027. Mecklenburg now revalues on a four-year cycle, and 2023 was the last one. Expect notices and refreshed online records in early 2027. An informal review can be requested within 30 days of the notice date.

How do I pay a Charlotte property tax bill?

Use the card line at 1-800-994-1026, send an eCheck, mail a check to the City-County Tax Collector, or visit during weekday hours. Include the 24-digit bill number, since a payment without it is returned. Cards bring a vendor fee.

Can I appeal my Charlotte property value after the deadline?

Generally no. Each spring the board of equalization and review adjourns, and that date is the cutoff unless a notice of value change gave you a later one. The next broad opening follows the 2027 revaluation notices.

What happens to unpaid Charlotte property tax when I sell?

Closing takes it from your proceeds, with interest added once the bill is past January 5. The lien has attached to the parcel since January 1 of the tax year. Get the balance from the Mecklenburg Office of Tax Administration before you sign a contract.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Behind on Raleigh property tax?

Who bills a Raleigh homeowner

Wake County does. Under a local agreement, its Tax Administration department sends the bills for Raleigh and the county's other towns, so a Raleigh owner receives one statement carrying county and city charges.

That department also values land, buildings and business property. Call 919-856-5400 or write to taxhelp@wake.gov. Wake has 16 cities and towns, and a municipal rate is folded into each bill. Questions about how Raleigh set its own rate go to the city, not the county.

Raleigh property tax rates

The county rate is .5371 and the Raleigh rate is .3720, for a combined .9091 per $100 of value. Commissioners voted on June 1 for a fiscal year 2027 budget that raises the county rate to 53.71 cents.

Rates and fee example for a house inside Raleigh

Combined rate.9091 per $100
Waste reduction fee in the county example$20

The county's worked example for a house inside Raleigh and outside any fire or special district adds that $20 waste reduction fee. Where the parcel lies can add further lines:

  • Residential waste reduction fee, charged per living unit, so a duplex has two.
  • Fire district tax, where the property lies in one.
  • Special district tax, usually a downtown area designated by legislation.
  • Municipal fees such as stormwater or solid waste.
  • A vehicle fee for motor vehicles inside a municipality.

To see the exact charges for your address, use the county's online bill search or call the tax office.

Due dates, interest and partial payments

The county mails bills in July. Each one covers the fiscal year that starts July 1 and ends the next June 30. You can pay the face amount from September 1 through January 5 (G.S. 105-360).

After that, interest runs: 2 percent for January and an added 0.75 percent per month following. The county takes partial payments in any amount, with no prior approval, as long as the balance is paid in full by January 5. Short-term payment plans are possible. Call early, because the county cannot help once a bill is overdue. Past-due taxes can be collected from paychecks, bank accounts or rent under state law.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Who is billed when a Raleigh home sells mid-year?

It depends on the sale date. If you sold between January and June and keep no interest in the property, the July bill should go to the new owner, who is responsible for paying it.

If the sale falls after the July bill and before the January delinquency date, the county mails a statement for the unpaid tax to the new owner, and the seller may disregard the original notice. Wake real estate becomes subject to a tax lien each January 1, and the lien stays until every dollar is paid. If a lender paid last year's bill from escrow, no July statement arrives, so look the account up online. Tell the closing attorney how you want that year's bill divided, and request the balance from Wake County Tax Administration.

Tax relief for Raleigh owners

Wake County administers three state programs: senior and disabled, tax deferment, and disabled veteran. The county's tax relief pages explain who qualifies. The state deadline is June 1 each year, and late applications can be accepted for good cause through December 31, 2026. Not knowing the program existed is typically not good cause.

The underlying laws are the senior and disabled statute and the veteran statute. Wake County Tax Administration can say whether a window is open.

How to pay a Wake County tax bill

Online, by several routes: ACH or eCheck, PayPal, Venmo, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and credit cards from the four major networks. Bills can be looked up online without waiting for the mail.

Owners with escrow accounts get no mailed bill. Look online or call 919-856-5400. After each partial payment, Tax Administration sends a statement showing what remains.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Wake County revaluation schedule

The latest countywide revaluation has a January 1, 2024 effective date, and the next one is dated January 1, 2027. In March 2025 the Wake County Board of Commissioners voted to phase in a two-year cycle, so the first revaluation on that cycle is effective January 1, 2029.

Roughly 460,000 parcels are sorted into 5,400 neighborhoods that share market, economic and geographic traits. Appraisers price land and buildings from sales data, review the results in the field and the office, and compile them into a Schedule of Values that commissioners must approve. The state minimum is one revaluation every eight years, and shorter gaps keep value increases from arriving as one large jump.

Which values and rates sit behind the current bill?

Bills due September 1, 2026, and delinquent after January 5, 2027, rest on assessed values as of January 1, 2024, and the rates approved in June 2026. Bills due September 1, 2027 use values as of January 1, 2027 and the rates set in June 2027.

  • A bill is assessed value times a rate stated per $100 of value.
  • Revaluation changes values only. Elected county and town officials set the rate.
  • State law has local governments publish a revenue-neutral rate for comparison, though they need not adopt it.
  • The county's online real estate search shows your current value and the data behind it.

If your Wake County value or record looks wrong

The county plans to mail 2027 value notices in the week of January 19, 2027, when commissioners receive the results. Every owner may appeal to the county's review board, and instructions plus a portal link are due out in January 2027.

If the record itself is wrong, for example a wrong square footage figure or an outbuilding that is gone, file the county's online request form with your address or account number and any documents. An appraiser may need to visit, and you would be contacted. Tax Administration also plans a comparable sales tool in January, useful as evidence. The next level above the local board is the state commission (G.S. 105-290).

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Selling a Raleigh house with unpaid property tax

Get the balance in writing from Wake County Tax Administration and hand it to your closing attorney. An unpaid bill follows the house, so it has to be settled for the title to be clean.

Back taxes can be cleared out of a seller's proceeds at the sale. Another option is a payment plan before the January deadline. A direct cash purchase of a Raleigh house as-is can move quickly while interest runs. Whoever buys, have the payoff quote cover the day you close.

Frequently asked questions

Will Raleigh mail me a separate city tax bill?

No. A local agreement has Wake County collect the city's share together with its own, so the single bill comes from Wake County Tax Administration.

When does a late Raleigh bill begin to accrue interest?

Interest starts January 6 if the bill is not paid in full by January 5. It is 2 percent for January and 0.75 percent per month after that.

Does Wake County take installments?

Yes. Any partial amount is welcome with no prior approval, so long as the full balance is in by January 5. Payment plans are possible if you call early.

What are the current Raleigh tax rates?

The county rate is .5371 and the Raleigh rate is .3720, a combined .9091 per $100 of value. Fees and district taxes may add to your bill, so check your own account.

Who owes the July bill if I sold my Raleigh house in the spring?

If you sold between January and June and keep no interest, the new owner should receive the July bill and is responsible for paying it. Confirm at closing.

Who sends the bill for a Greensboro home

Guilford County, not the City of Greensboro, mails the bill, and the city levy rides on the same statement. The Guilford County Tax Department keeps counters at 400 W. Market St. in Greensboro and 325 E. Russell Ave. in High Point, both open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Friday.

Dial 336-641-4814 about values and appeals. To arrange paying a balance in full before the delinquent date, use 336-641-3363. Greensboro sets its own levy, and the county's table shows it on a separate line.

Lenders that escrow request your bill each summer and send you a notice. Under North Carolina law, getting the tax paid is still the owner's job, so if the lender named on that notice is not yours, forward it to the right servicer.

Tax rates inside Greensboro

For 2026-2027 the countywide rate is 0.78950 and the City of Greensboro rate is 0.79850, for a total of 1.58800 under rate code 01. Rates are fractions of $1 for each $100 of value.

Guilford County 2026-2027 rates for Greensboro parcels

01 Greensboro0.789500.798501.58800
19 Greensboro, Dunleath Historic District0.789500.05000 added1.63800

Code 01 covers most city parcels. Parcels in the Dunleath and College Hill historic districts and the downtown improvement district carry an extra district charge, so read the code on your bill. A $30 vehicle fee also applies in Greensboro and is neither discounted nor penalized.

Senate Bill 889 and your bill

The law froze use of the 2026 reappraisal values for one year, so bills for the fiscal year that began July 1, 2026 rest on the older values. The moratorium covers the county's revaluation process. It does not stop local governments from changing their rates.

  • Greensboro adopted its fiscal year 2026-27 budget in June, with a total city rate of 79.85 cents.
  • The city describes that as a 12.6-cent adjustment on current property values, not on the new reappraisal values.
  • The updated values are paused until January 1, 2027, and are expected to feed the budget year that begins July 1, 2027.

Your new notice of value does not set this year's bill. It still matters, because if the value is wrong the appeal clock runs on it, and an appeal that stays open now is considered for the 2027 tax year.

Due dates and how to pay

The bill is due September 1 and stays free of interest through January 5 (G.S. 105-360). After that, interest is 2% for the first month and 0.75% on the first of every month that follows.

  • Discount: Guilford County and Greensboro each give 1.0% off for payment before September 1.
  • Online, or by phone at (336) 203-7795: 1.85% processing charge and a $2 transaction fee.
  • At a tax office counter: cash and checks are free, while a card carries 2.35% and $2.
  • Mail: Guilford County Tax Department, P.O. Box 70939, Charlotte, NC 28272-0939.

The USPS postmark fixes the date of a mailed payment, and proving it was on time falls to you. The county phones about payment only when a bill is delinquent, and gift cards are never accepted.

How to appeal your assessment

Send the appeal to the Guilford County Tax Department. Filings for 2026 are accepted through December 31, 2026, and filings for 2027 through May 17, 2027. The online portal opens January 1, 2027.

If you already appealed the reappraisal value, you do not need to refile, because that appeal carries into tax year 2027.

For a paper form, hand it to a postal clerk for a hand-cancelled postmark. A mailbox drop can be stamped the next day with no proof, and anything postmarked after May 17 is rejected. Before the portal opens, request a form at taxreval@guilfordcountync.gov.

The board hears whatever staff cannot settle. The next stop is the state Property Tax Commission, with notice due 30 days after the board mails its decision (G.S. 105-290). Personal property is a separate track with its own 30-day window from the notice date.

Tax relief for homeowners

Greensboro homeowners may use any of three state programs, with a June 1 filing deadline each year. Mail applications to Guilford County Tax Department, PO Box 3138, Greensboro, NC 27402, or carry them to either tax office.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: $25,000 or half the value, whichever is more, off the home of a qualifying 65-plus or disabled owner whose gross income stays under $38,800. One application is enough.
  • Circuit breaker: the tax is held to 4% or 5% of income, using caps of $38,800 and $58,200, after five years of owning and living in the home. It is renewed annually.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of value, with no age or income test, applied for once.

Only one program per owner is allowed. A late application is still reviewed if it arrives at least one week before the last equalization board meeting in December. Questions go to 336-641-3320 or 336-641-7911. A circuit breaker owner who sells owes the last three years of deferred tax, with interest, on the sale date.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed

Interest starts, collection begins at once, and the tax stays a lien on the parcel. Tools include wage and bank garnishment, levies on personal property, attachment of state refunds and lottery winnings, and foreclosure on real estate.

Under G.S. 105-355 the lien dates from the listing date and includes penalties and costs. A foreclosure action under G.S. 105-374 ends at a courthouse-door auction, and redemption before confirmation requires paying taxes, interest, penalties and costs. Guilford holds no tax lien sales.

Before listing, ask the tax department for the figures on the current bill. A deferred balance under a relief program is a separate item, so ask for it by name. A cash buyer will still expect the title to be clear, so the tax has to be settled at or before closing.

Greensboro housing

Greensboro has 308,667 residents and 123,984 households, averaging 2.29 people. About 50.5% of homes are owner-occupied, so owners and renters are nearly even and a sale often has a landlord on one side. The middle value of an owner's home is $244,800, middle gross rent is $1,172, and middle owner costs with a mortgage are $1,447 a month, a baseline to hold against your own tax line. When you list, have the current bill, your rate code and any relief approval letter ready for the buyer's agent.

Frequently asked questions

Which government mails the Greensboro tax statement?

Guilford County. Its tax department bills the county and city levies together from counters at 400 W. Market St., Greensboro, and 325 E. Russell Ave., High Point.

What total rate does a city parcel carry?

Rate code 01 totals 1.58800 for 2026-2027, made of 0.78950 countywide plus 0.79850 for Greensboro. Historic and downtown districts add more.

Does Greensboro reward early payers?

Yes. Guilford County and Greensboro each allow a 1.0% discount for paying before September 1.

Is an appeal still possible after the moratorium?

Yes. Guilford accepts 2026 appeals through December 31, 2026, and 2027 appeals through May 17, 2027, with its online portal starting January 1, 2027. Earlier appeals stay active.

Does Guilford County auction tax liens to investors?

No. The tax department conducts no tax lien sales, though it enforces collection with garnishment and real estate foreclosure.

Where Winston-Salem owners take tax questions

A Winston-Salem home is taxed through Forsyth County Tax Administration, which handles appeals, relief applications and ownership questions. Visit 201 N. Chestnut Street, inside the Forsyth County Government Center, or call 336-703-2300. Appeal and relief forms are available at that counter.

Before you call, write down the parcel number so the clerk can pull your file in one step. The county's real estate page suggests having the parcel number, the owner's full name and the street address ready before you call the appraisal section. Appraisal records can be bought for 50 cents a page. If you want to know how a city levy shows up on your bill, ask the tax office.

Winston-Salem housing at a glance

Winston-Salem is home to about 257,271 people as of 2025, a 3.1% increase from 249,549 in April 2020, on roughly 133 square miles.

  • Just over half of homes (55.6%) are owner-occupied, so close to half are rentals.
  • A typical owned home is worth $233,800, and gross rent is typically $1,087.
  • Monthly owner costs run a median $1,459 with a mortgage and $486 without.

The 2020 count works out to about 1,880 residents on each of the city's 132.7 square miles of land, so values vary a lot from block to block. Your own street may look nothing like these city-wide averages, and a house in need of repairs can carry an assessed value above what it would fetch. Check the assessment before you list. Anyone weighing the cost of holding a vacant house should add the tax bill, insurance and upkeep to the averages above.

Due dates and penalties

The September 1 due date is followed by a grace period, and face value payments are accepted through the day before January 6. From January 6 interest is 2% until February begins, then three-fourths of a percent every month. A mailed check is judged by its USPS postmark date.

Sellers should know who gets the bill: the January 1 titleholder. If you close later in the year, you are still the liable party on paper. The closing usually prorates the tax, and the county advises confirming with your realtor or attorney that it was done.

How to appeal your assessment

Put your appeal to the Forsyth County review board in writing, using the form from the Tax Office. It must arrive or be postmarked after January 1 and no later than the last business day in June. The form is online and at the Tax Office.

The board follows state hearing rules. A reappraisal year can shift the calendar, so confirm the date with the office before you file. If you want to challenge the value, decide before you list, because the window closes in the middle of the selling season. Gather recent nearby sales, repair estimates and photos, and attach them to the written appeal so the board has something concrete to weigh.

Tax relief programs

Forsyth County administers three relief programs, and an owner may use just one of them. The cutoff for applications is June 1 every year.

North Carolina relief programs available to Winston-Salem owners

You can get an application from the Tax Office or online. For a home with several non-spouse owners, all of them must meet the standards for the circuit breaker.

Back tax on a Winston-Salem house

An unpaid bill stays attached to the house. The lien takes hold on the January 1 listing date, and penalties, interest and costs pile on beside it. If it goes unpaid long enough the county can seek a court-ordered sale, and selling first avoids that. Owners who inherit a house should look for back years too, since each year adds its own lien and interest. Have the Tax Office list every open year on the parcel so the payoff is complete. The closing agent pays it out of your proceeds.

  • Request the exact balance on your parcel from Forsyth County.
  • Make sure the attorney lists it on the settlement sheet.
  • File proof of payment with your closing papers.

Growth and who stays

Forsyth County also covers owners outside the city limits, so make sure the bill and records you pull are for your own parcel. The city grew from 229,617 residents in the 2010 census to 249,545 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate is 257,271. Roughly 85.3% of residents stayed at the same address over the prior year, a settled population in which many owners have held their homes for years. Such owners may not have seen a market price in a long time, which makes recent nearby sales worth checking against your assessment.

A disabled owner who meets the state test may qualify for the $45,000 exclusion, and the Tax Office can explain the steps.

Circuit breaker deferrals and a sale

A deferral becomes a lien, so it has to be cleared when the house sells. Under the circuit breaker program, the part of the tax above the income cap is deferred. That amount accrues interest and is added to the property as a lien.

If you qualify, ask the Tax Office for the full deferred balance before listing. It shows up in the title search, and the closing agent pays it from your proceeds. The program also requires five years of owning and occupying the home, and a new application each year.

  • Income of $38,800 or less pays 4% of income.
  • Income above that, up to $58,200, pays 5% of income.
  • Any tax above those amounts is deferred and carries interest.

Planning a sale around tax dates

Line up your closing with the tax year. A spring closing happens after the date that fixed the owner, so the seller's name sits on that year's bill even when the buyer moves in during March.

An inherited or empty house follows the same rule, and unpaid amounts keep growing through interest. Before you list, call the Tax Office at 336-703-2300, get the balance, and settle with the buyer on who pays what. If the closing lands in the weeks after the bill goes out, the buyer will likely want a copy of it for their own records.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What to do before closing

  1. Get the parcel number and the current balance from Forsyth County.
  2. Ask whether any relief deferral is on the account.
  3. Check that your attorney's settlement sheet prorates the bill.
  4. Keep the receipt with your closing papers.

A cash buyer still expects the tax to be handled at closing, so these steps apply however the sale is financed, though a cash deal skips the lender's appraisal and can close sooner.

Frequently asked questions

Which number reaches Winston-Salem's tax office?

Call Forsyth County Tax Administration at 336-703-2300. The office is in the Forsyth County Government Center at 201 N. Chestnut Street.

When does a Winston-Salem appeal window end?

The last business day in June. Check with the office about the year you are filing, since a reappraisal year can shift the calendar.

Will I owe tax after a spring sale?

Possibly. The bill carries the January 1 owner's name, and the closing normally splits the cost between buyer and seller.

When does interest start on unpaid Winston-Salem tax?

Interest starts on January 6, at 2% until February 1 and three-fourths of a percent per month after that.

Can I get a lower tax bill as a senior or a disabled veteran?

Maybe. All three state programs need an application and cannot be stacked. Ask whether you meet the age, disability or veteran tests, since the answer changes which one fits.

Who bills property tax in Fayetteville

If you are selling a house in Fayetteville, the office to know is Cumberland Tax Administration, which belongs to the county. It sets the value, sends the statement and collects payment. The city levies its own rate, yet both levies print together on the county's single bill.

Visit 117 Dick Street, Room 530, Fayetteville, NC 28301, or phone 910-678-7507. Letters should be addressed to Cumberland Tax Administration, PO Box 449, Fayetteville NC 28302. City rate, county rate and any city fees all sit on one statement. Because of that, a closing agent will ask for your parcel number before quoting a payoff, so have it handy.

Rates and fees on the bill

Two rates and a handful of flat fees make up the bill: 49.9 cents per $100 of value for the county, 44.95 cents per $100 for the city, and set charges for trash and stormwater. The county's rate page covers the 2026 tax bills (fiscal year 2027) and prints each levy as a decimal, with 0.9485 as the combined city figure. A house just outside the city line is billed a different mix, which includes a fire district charge and a recreation rate.

Levies on Fayetteville 2026 tax bills
LevyAmount
County ad valorem rate0.499
City of Fayetteville rate0.4495
Combined city and county rate0.9485
Fayetteville Revitalization District0.1489 + 0.4495, combined 1.0974
City solid waste fee, residential units with seven or fewer units$285 a year
City residential stormwater fee$84, $168 or $252 a year by impervious area tier
City vehicle fee and transit tax$25 and $5 per registered vehicle

Impervious surface decides the stormwater tier: tier 1 is under 2,500 square feet, tier 2 covers 2,501 to 4,800 square feet, and tier 3 is larger than that.

  • Stormwater, solid waste, refuse, recycling and transit charges sit outside the combined rate, so your real total runs higher.
  • A parcel inside the revitalization district pays an extra levy beyond the city rate.

Due dates and interest

The bill is dated for September 1. Nothing extra accrues until January 6, so January 5 is your real deadline. Owners who sell in the fall should settle the bill before then.

These dates come from G.S. 105-360, which applies everywhere in the state. Money received before January 6 settles the bill at face value. On January 6 the balance picks up 2 percent for the rest of January, and every month or partial month beyond that adds three-fourths of one percent. Owners who need to split the bill can call 910-678-7507 and ask about installments.

If you sell, ask the closing attorney to check that the payoff covers this year's bill. Recording a deed does not erase unpaid tax. The lien belongs to the land and travels to the buyer. See G.S. 105-355 for how the lien works.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

The 2025 revaluation

Cumberland reappraised every parcel at its January 1, 2025 market value, replacing the 2017 figures. The eight year ceiling between reappraisals is a state rule. County staff describe the purpose as fairness among properties rather than a larger or smaller total levy. Rates for the new values began July 1, 2025.

Think of the reappraisal as the baseline your buyer will see. A fresh assessed figure is public, so buyers' agents will look at it and compare it with your asking price. If the number looks high, the informal review below is the cheapest place to argue it. If you already hold an approved relief application, you keep it and do not refile. The exemption itself continues, though the dollar amount on your bill moves with the new value.

Where do I send a challenge to my Fayetteville value?

Begin with an informal Request for Review sent to Tax Administration. A dispute that survives that step moves to the Board of Equalization and Review.

  • Informal review: the request can be filed online, mailed, emailed, handed in at Room 530 of the county courthouse (117 Dick Street) or left in the secure drop box in the back lot. Attach recent comparable sales or other proof of value.
  • Deadline: informal appeals for the 2027 tax year are due February 5, 2027, and you should expect a decision letter around April 2027.
  • Board hearing: if the informal stage does not settle it, take the case to the Board of Equalization and Review. Call the office for this year's adjournment date.
  • Further appeal: send written notice to the state Property Tax Commission within 30 days after the board mails its ruling (G.S. 105-290).

For a mailed request, address it to Attn: Real Estate Assessment at the PO Box above. List a phone number and mailing address that work, since an appraiser may arrange to visit the house. If you sell before the review ends, tell the office so the letter reaches the right person.

Relief programs

A homeowner picks among three state programs and gets only one: the senior or disability exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion, or the circuit breaker cap. Check these before you list, since each changes what the county will say is owed at transfer.

  • Elderly or disabled owners whose 2026 income is $38,800 or below can exclude $25,000 of value, or half of it when half is the bigger number (G.S. 105-277.1).
  • The disabled veteran exclusion removes $45,000 from the taxed value and ignores age and income (G.S. 105-277.1C).
  • Under the circuit breaker, the bill is limited to 4 percent of income, or 5 percent where income falls between $38,800 and $58,200. Whatever exceeds the cap is deferred as a lien (G.S. 105-277.1B).

Form AV-9 goes to the county assessor. January is best, and June 1 before the tax year is the last day. Selling ends a circuit breaker deferral and brings three years of deferred tax due at once, so get that number from the county before you take an offer.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed

Back taxes come out of your proceeds at the closing table. The lien attached to the parcel on January 1, the listing date, so the buyer's lender will want it cleared.

  1. Ask the county for a written payoff that adds in interest and city fees.
  2. Hand it to your closing attorney well ahead of the signing appointment.
  3. Find out if a circuit breaker deferral is attached to the parcel.
  4. Let the attorney pay the county from your proceeds.
  5. Keep the paid receipt with your closing papers.

Once January 5 passes with the bill open, the county may sue to foreclose its lien. Selling the house first is the simplest cure, since the payoff comes out of the price. Foreclosure under G.S. 105-374 ends with an auction at the courthouse door. An owner who redeems before the sale is confirmed pays the taxes, penalties, interest and costs.

Fayetteville is a renter-heavy market: 47.4 percent of homes are owner occupied (2020 to 2024), and the median value of those homes is $188,000. Median gross rent is $1,250. Many sellers here are landlords, and a rented house is liened just like an owner's home. A cash buyer still sees the same payoff.

Paperwork to gather before listing

A short folder saves days at closing. Pull together your parcel number, your most recent statement from Cumberland Tax Administration, and any approval letter for a relief program you use. If you filed an informal review that is still open, add that paperwork too.

Then call 910-678-7507 and ask what the payoff would be on a given date. Interest and city fees change the figure from week to week, so request it close to your signing day and ask for it in writing. Your closing attorney needs that sheet to wire the county its share, and the title company will hold up the deed until the tax lien is accounted for. Keep a copy of the paid receipt in your records once the county has been paid, in case a later bill is questioned.

Frequently asked questions

Who do I call about my Fayetteville tax statement?

Call Cumberland County Tax Administration at 910-678-7507, or go to Room 530 at 117 Dick Street. Values, bills and payment plans all run through that one desk.

What day does interest start on a Fayetteville bill?

January 6. Pay by January 5 to avoid it. Then 2 percent applies through February 1, and each later month adds three-fourths of one percent.

What combined rate applies inside Fayetteville city limits?

0.9485 for 2026, which is 0.4495 from the city plus 0.499 from the county. Trash, stormwater and vehicle charges come on top.

Is there still time to appeal a Fayetteville assessment?

For the 2027 tax year, informal requests are due February 5, 2027. Formal appeals follow at the Board of Equalization and Review.

If I sell with tax unpaid, does the debt go with the house?

It can, since the lien belongs to the land. Most sellers have the closing attorney pay it off at closing so the buyer starts clean.

Which government bills a Cary home for property tax?

The county does, not the town. Town limits now reach into Wake, Chatham and Durham counties. Whichever county holds the parcel values it, bills it and collects the town's tax along with its own.

Your parcel's location decides which county applies, and your bill or the county's online search will tell you. These are the numbers to use:

  • Wake County Tax Administration, 919-856-5400. Walk-in help is at 301 S. McDowell St., Suite 3800, Raleigh, weekdays 8:30 to 5:00.
  • Chatham County Collection Division, 919-542-8250.
  • Durham County Tax Administrator, 919-560-0300.

Under a local agreement Wake mails the bills and takes in payment for every town and special district within the county. A Cary owner in Wake pays one bill with the county and town rates together. Questions about how the town rate was set go to the town. The town also adds a $30 vehicle license fee that rides on the vehicle tax bill, with no sticker.

Cary and Wake County tax rates

For fiscal year 2027 the town rate is 36.75 cents per $100 and the Wake County rate is 53.71 cents per $100. A bill adds the two when the parcel is in Wake.

The Cary Town Council adopted its budget raising the town rate by 2.75 cents. The budget also sets a solid waste and recycling fee of $28 per month. That is billed on its own and is not part of the property tax rate. Wake's commissioners raised the county rate by 2 cents to reach 53.71 cents.

The rates are multiplied by assessed value, which makes that value as important as either rate. After a revaluation the rate can move in either direction. Chatham and Durham County parcels carry those counties' own rates, which you can get from the numbers above. Rates reset every July 1 with the budgets, so rely on the current bill instead of last year's figure.

Due dates and payment

Taxes are due September 1. Anything paid by January 5 carries no extra charge. Interest begins January 6 under G.S. 105-360.

Property tax calendar
StepRule
Listing periodFirst business day of January through January 31
Taxes dueSeptember 1
No interestThrough January 5

You can pay Wake in pieces of any size with no approval needed, so long as the balance is cleared by January 5. A statement showing what remains follows each payment. If your lender pays through escrow, no paper bill is mailed to you, and the online lookup shows the amount. Wake takes ACH or eCheck, PayPal, Venmo, Apple Pay, Google Pay and the four major credit cards.

How revaluation affects a Cary home's value

Wake's last reappraisal took effect January 1, 2024. The next is effective January 1, 2027, and a two-year cycle follows. State law requires a reappraisal only every eighth year, so Wake revalues far more often than the minimum.

Wake works through neighborhooding, sales-based pricing of land and buildings, field and office review, and finally the notice of assessment with its appeal review. The county sorts about 460,000 parcels into 5,400 neighborhoods, and its commissioners approve the resulting Schedule of Values. The 2027 schedule has results before the Board on January 19, 2027, value notices out by January 22, 2027, and an appeal deadline planned for April 30, 2027.

If you dispute the notice, take the case to the county's review board. A loss at the board leads to the Property Tax Commission. Notice must be filed within 30 days of the mailed decision, as G.S. 105-290 sets out. Wake runs a call center for questions on the 2027 round at 919-857-3800.

Tax relief for Cary homeowners

Wake County runs three state programs for Cary owners in its portion: the Senior and Disabled Program, Tax Deferment and the Disabled Veteran Program. The programs cover low-income owners 65 and older, low-income owners who are 100% disabled, and those with a total, permanent service-connected disability, along with unmarried surviving spouses.

  • Age or disability: the 2026 income limit is $38,800, and a qualifying home loses whichever is more, $25,000 or half its appraised value, from the taxable amount.
  • Disabled veteran: $45,000 of appraised value comes off, with no age or income limit.
  • Circuit breaker: after five years of owning and living in the home, the bill is limited to 4.0% of income, or 5.0% where income is above $38,800 and at most $58,200.

State law sets June 1. Wake looks at late applications one by one, for good cause, through December 31 of the same year. Forgetting or not knowing about a program is typically not good cause. Wake's examples that do count are illness, a death in the immediate family, military deployment and a delay in getting disability certification. An owner gets one program, not a stack, so ask the tax office which one fits. G.S. 105-277.1 has the exclusion rules.

What if I cannot pay my Cary property tax?

Call Wake County Tax Administration at 919-856-5400 before January 6. Wake can set up short-term payment plans, earlier calls leave more options, and it cannot help once a bill becomes overdue.

State law permits past due taxes to be taken from paychecks, bank accounts or rent. The parcel lien arises under G.S. 105-355 as of the listing date. Foreclosure under G.S. 105-374 finishes with an auction at the courthouse door, though redemption remains possible before confirmation.

If a Cary house also has a mortgage in default, the tax lien and the lender's foreclosure can run at the same time, which narrows the timeline. If you sell before an auction, the price stays with you, minus the tax paid at closing.

Selling a Cary home

Cary had an estimated 183,582 people in July 2025. Owned homes had a median value of $580,200 across 2020-2024, and two in three units, 66.6%, are lived in by their owners.

Sequence matters. First work out which county holds the parcel, then call it for the balance on every bill, find out whether a relief claim or deferral is on file, and hand the written figures to the closing attorney. If taxes are behind, the county's short-term payment plan is worth a call before listing, since options shrink once a bill is overdue.

Check your value notice after each revaluation, since assessed value is half of the tax calculation. At listing time, get a payoff figure from whichever county holds your parcel. The closing attorney then pays that year's open tax from what you receive. Recording happens at that same county's register of deeds. Wake's register sets the excise tax at $2 per thousand dollars of price. With a cash buyer there is no lender escrow to unwind, and the tax is simply settled at the table.

Frequently asked questions

Which county do I pay Cary property tax to?

Pay the county that holds your parcel: Wake, Chatham or Durham. Wake, Chatham and Durham each assess, bill and collect for the parcels inside their own borders, town tax included.

What is the Cary town property tax rate?

For fiscal year 2027 the town charges 36.75 cents per $100 of assessed value, a 2.75 cent increase. Wake County's rate is 53.71 cents per $100, and Wake collects both for parcels in its portion.

When does Wake County interest begin on Cary taxes?

It begins January 6, so paying by January 5 avoids it. The charge is 2% to February 1, then three-fourths of a percent monthly.

When is the next Wake County revaluation?

January 1, 2027, with a two-year rhythm after that. Wake plans to send value notices by January 22, 2027.

Can a Cary senior reduce a property tax bill?

Possibly, if age or disability and income tests are met. The exclusion removes $25,000 or half the value, whichever is bigger. File by June 1, though late filings can be weighed for good cause.
